      "partial_result": "## Verdict: accept the binder at the source level. I found no contract blocker for immutable bytes \u2192 detached metadata.\n\nI didn't run any tests or edit any repository files. The only things I executed were hash checks and one standard-library `json` check that doesn't touch the repo. I did save a short note of this verdict to my memory folder outside the repo.\n\n**What I checked:**\n- **Frozen files:** both match the given hashes (`102ab0ab\u2026` for the source, `c5dc648c\u2026` for the test) and are identical to the worker's copies.\n- **Helpers:** `connected_gallery_provenance.py`, `connected_gallery_conversion.py` and the fixture test are byte-identical between the worker's base (a2deea75), master (2b680c90) and the worker's worktree.\n- **Real fragment:** every member of the genuine fragment is well under 64 MiB (largest is `origin-export.json` at 6.18 MB), and it has 1,715 rows, so it passes the size bound and the ten-row minimum.\n\n**Contract items, all satisfied:**\n- **All seven pins before any JSON (lines 58\u201387):** the dicts are copied first (lines 64\u201365), key and value types must be exact builtins, the key sets must match exactly, and then the serving bytes and all six fragments are hashed. No parse happens before this.\n- **Size and encoding (lines 88\u201395):** the 64 MiB limit, strict UTF-8 and the NUL check run on all five JSON inputs before the first `_parse`. The limit is inclusive, which matches the repo's existing 64 MiB checks in scripts; there's nothing in `src` to reuse.\n- **Producer rebuilt from the originals (line 110):** `bind_gallery_provenance` is called with the snapshotted bytes and pins of `origin-export.json` and `origin.json`.\n- **Canonical selection and IDs (lines 151 and 155):** `gallery-ids.json` and `gallery-provenance.json` must equal, byte for byte, the canonical versions built from the fresh producer. That is what rejects the four repinned mutants (encoder, batch, rows, null hash), and the RED log shows they were accepted before this check existed.\n- **Payload files (line 136):** each payload SHA is compared by name against the original bundle's file list. Payload sizes are only checked to be non-negative integers, as intended for expected values.\n- **Fragment files (lines 133\u2013134):** each fragment record's size and SHA must match the actual supplied bytes.\n- **Exact keys and types:** `_same` compares canonical encodings, so `true` and `33.0` are rejected, along with extra or missing keys.\n- **`encoder_binding_sha256` (lines 176\u2013180):** it is only the digest of `{identity, gallery_batches, gallery_rows}`, and the test confirms `fixed_sha256` is rejected in its place.\n- **Detached result:** both returned dicts are freshly parsed, and the only module globals are immutable tuples.\n- **Owners file:** hashed and never parsed. `gallery.bin` is never compared against the combined wire, which is deliberate.\n\n## Test gaps (not blockers; the implementation is correct in each case)\n\n1. **A file-record swap isn't tested** (line 136 for payloads, 133\u2013134 for fragments).\n   - **Problem:** a mutant that checks `digest in payload_files.values()` instead of matching by name survives. The payload test uses a SHA that isn't in the bundle at all, and the fixture gives `vision.pt` and `endpoint.pt` the same hash. The same mutant on fragment records also survives (the tests use `\"0\"*64` and size 0).\n   - **Smallest falsifier:** set `files[\"processor.json\"].sha256` to the bundle's `vision.pt` SHA, and swap the `sha256`/`bytes` of the `origin.json` and `origin-export.json` records. Both must reject.\n\n2. **The size/UTF-8 gate is only proven for two of the five JSON inputs** (lines 88\u201395).\n   - **Problem:** removing `origin-export.json`, `gallery-ids.json` or `gallery-provenance.json` from the `_json_bytes` tuple survives. The 64 MiB sentinel only covers the serving manifest and `origin.json`, and the UTF-16/32 cases only cover the serving manifest. The bad-JSON fragment cases are rejected later by `_parse` or the byte comparison anyway.\n   - **Smallest falsifier:** run the existing `len` sentinel for all four fragment JSON names with `assertRaisesRegex(\"JSON exceeds 64 MiB\")`.\n\n3. **The unique-ID check is never run** (line 149). The genuine fixture never has duplicate `relative_path` values, and the duplicate-ID test is rejected by the canonical byte comparison instead. The batch-membership check (lines 139\u2013147) can't be reached when the producer is genuine. Both are harmless leftovers copied from the converter.\n\n## Remaining limits (not blockers)\n\n- **Byte-order mark:** a UTF-8 BOM in front of the serving manifest or an origin JSON is accepted, because `json.loads` on bytes decodes it as `utf-8-sig` (I confirmed this on 3.14.4). JSON's spec allows parsers to ignore a BOM, and pinning makes it harmless, but a non-Python reader shouldn't assume the pinned files are BOM-free.\n- **Deep nesting:** very deeply nested JSON raises `RecursionError`, not `ValueError`. This comes from the existing `_parse`. It still refuses the input, but by crashing rather than with a clean `ValueError`.\n- **Where the pins come from:** the binder has no content check on `gallery.bin`. A caller who repins `gallery.bin` and regenerates the provenance around the genuine producer will be accepted. So whoever calls it must take the six fragment pins from the frozen fragment authority (`gallery.bin` 386f3b22\u2026, IDs df9fb988\u2026, provenance 11e6fbc9\u2026, receipt db63db82\u2026, bundle e12429ef\u2026, owners 8e38d2e5\u2026). They must never come from `serving.json`'s own file records, and the serving pin must be frozen by the parent.\n- **Full test run still owed:** `source-review-v3.json` says the tests weren't rerun after the final change.
